Plays the music on this phone and on your own music server, and internet radio. It can also search, stream and download songs from YouTube Music.

Your library, playlists, queue, hearts and settings stay on this phone. A music server\'s password (for Jellyfin, the sign-in it hands back instead; the password is not kept) and a YouTube sign-in are sealed with a key in the phone\'s keystore before they are saved. Nothing is sent to the app\'s maker.

The app goes online only for what you use: your own music server (Navidrome or another Subsonic server, or Jellyfin) at the address you type in, and nowhere else, each request carrying your sign-in to it; YouTube Music, to search, stream and download, and, if you switch on Keep playing similar songs, to ask what plays next; radio.garden, to browse stations (and Radio Browser, when a search finds nothing there), and each station\'s own stream while it plays; api.zippopotam.us, only for a US or Canadian postal code typed into the radio search; musicbrainz.org, only if you switch on Fill in album details from MusicBrainz, to look up albums whose tags leave gaps (their title and artist are sent). A server on a home network is often plain http, so what goes to it is not encrypted.

This app is free software under the GNU General Public License v3. It comes with no warranty: use it at your own risk. YouTube, radio stations and music servers are run by others, under their own terms.

This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little: what you put in stays on this phone unless you send it somewhere yourself. The only things that go out are the requests described above: your searches, plays, downloads and sign-in to YouTube Music; requests for stations and their streams to radio.garden; the words of a radio search to Radio Browser; a ZIP or postal code to Zippopotam.us; requests to your own music server, if you add one; and, only if you turn it on, an album\'s title and artist to MusicBrainz. Nothing comes to the developer.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: remove songs, playlists and stations in the app, save your playlists and stations with Save a backup, delete downloaded songs in Music/Music Box (ordinary files that stay after an uninstall), clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What YouTube Music, radio.garden, Radio Browser, Zippopotam.us and MusicBrainz receive is covered by their own privacy policies. A server of your own is yours: what it keeps is up to you.
